## Project setup

Before you start building you need to set up the Database and API. You can do this by starting a new Project in Supabase and then creating a "schema" inside the database.

### Create a project

1. [Create a new project](/dashboard) in the Supabase Dashboard.
2. Enter your project details.
3. Wait for the new database to launch.

### Set up the database schema

Now set up the database schema. You can use the "User Management Starter" quickstart in the SQL Editor, or you can copy/paste the SQL from below and run it.

<Tabs
  scrollable
  size="small"
  type="underlined"
  defaultActiveId="dashboard"
  queryGroup="database-method"
>
<TabPanel id="dashboard" label="Dashboard">

1. Go to the [SQL Editor](/dashboard/project/_/sql) page in the Dashboard.
2. Click **User Management Starter** under the **Reference > Examples** tab.
3. Click **Run**.

<Admonition type="note">

You can pull the database schema down to your local project by running the `db pull` command. Read the [local development docs](/docs/guides/local-development/database-migrations#link-your-project) for detailed instructions.

```bash
supabase link --project-ref <project-id>
# You can get <project-id> from your project's dashboard URL: https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/<project-id>
supabase db pull
```

</Admonition>

</TabPanel>
<TabPanel id="sql" label="SQL">

<Admonition type="note">

When working locally you can run the following command to create a new migration file:

</Admonition>

```bash
supabase migration new user_management_starter
```

</TabPanel>

1	```sql
2	-- Create a table for public profiles
3	create table profiles (
4	  id uuid references auth.users not null primary key,
5	  updated_at timestamp with time zone,
6	  username text unique,
7	  full_name text,
8	  avatar_url text,
9	  website text,
10	
11	  constraint username_length check (char_length(username) >= 3)
12	);
13	
14	-- Grant the privileges roles need
15	GRANT SELECT ON public.profiles TO anon;
16	GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON public.profiles TO authenticated;
17	
18	-- Set up Row Level Security (RLS)
19	-- See https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security for more details.
20	alter table profiles
21	  enable row level security;
22	
23	create policy "Public profiles are viewable by everyone." on profiles
24	  for select using (true);
25	
26	create policy "Users can insert their own profile." on profiles
27	  for insert with check ((select auth.uid()) = id);
28	
29	create policy "Users can update own profile." on profiles
30	  for update using ((select auth.uid()) = id);
31	
32	-- This trigger automatically creates a profile entry when a new user signs up via Supabase Auth.
33	-- See https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/managing-user-data#using-triggers for more details.
34	create function public.handle_new_user()
35	returns trigger
36	set search_path = ''
37	as $$
38	begin
39	  insert into public.profiles (id, full_name, avatar_url)
40	  values (new.id, new.raw_user_meta_data->>'full_name', new.raw_user_meta_data->>'avatar_url');
41	  return new;
42	end;
43	$$ language plpgsql security definer;
44	create trigger on_auth_user_created
45	  after insert on auth.users
46	  for each row execute procedure public.handle_new_user();
47	
48	-- Set up Storage!
49	insert into storage.buckets (id, name)
50	  values ('avatars', 'avatars');
51	
52	-- Set up access controls for storage. Allows downloading object with public key
53	-- See https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/security/access-control#policy-examples for more details.
54	create policy "Avatar images are publicly accessible." on storage.objects
55	  for select using (bucket_id = 'avatars' and storage.allow_any_operation(array['object.get_authenticated_info', 'object.get_authenticated']));
56	
57	create policy "Anyone can upload an avatar." on storage.objects
58	  for insert with check (bucket_id = 'avatars');
59	
60	create policy "Anyone can update their own avatar." on storage.objects
61	  for update using ((select auth.uid()) = owner) with check (bucket_id = 'avatars');
62	```

content.text:
Found it — that's expected behavior, not a bug.

The `handle_new_user()` trigger (`apps/docs/content/_partials/user_management_quickstart_sql_template.mdx`, lines 32–46) is defined as `on_auth_user_created`, which fires `AFTER INSERT ON auth.users` only. It does not run on `UPDATE`, so updating `auth.users` won't trigger it or sync changes to `public.profiles`.

To have it also run on updates, you'd need a separate trigger with `AFTER UPDATE ON auth.users` (or add `OR UPDATE` to the existing trigger) calling a function that updates the matching `profiles` row.
